summary: Initial discovery focused on Summit Financial's data residency and compliance constraints. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment modes for PII/regulated workloads. Key concerns: GDPR data residency, audit/logging retention, encryption/KMS, egress controls, and contractual obligations for auditability. Redwood AE/SE explained architecture options and agreed to send security docs and schedule a technical benchmark.
topics: Data residency requirements (EU/US), HIPAA applicability for certain product lines, SOC2/ISO documentation, KMS/HSM integration, VPC/on-prem options, logging & PII redaction, timelines for pilot and procurement
questions: Can Redwood guarantee EU-only residency for specific datasets? How are audit logs handled for Private vs Dedicated vs Hosted? What encryption keys control customer data, and can we integrate with our HSM? What's the recommended rollout strategy for latency-sensitive features?
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-09
Start time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood SE), Karen Miles (CISO, Summit), Tom Reyes (Head of Cloud, Summit), Liam O'Neil (Senior Counsel), Rhea Patel (Platform Engineer)

Summary (auto-generated): initial compliance/discovery on data residency and deployment modes; follow-ups on security docs and a tech benchmark.

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time. quick round robin, I am Alex Chen, I'm the AE on the account. Priya and Jordan from our SE team here. how about you, Karen?
[00:18] Karen Miles: Hi alex, Karen Miles, CISO at Summit. Tom and Liam are with me, Rhea from platform as well — mainly here to clarify residency and logging rules.
[00:30] Alex Chen: Great — goal for today is to understand your residency/compliance constraints and figure out whether Hosted, Dedicated, or Private makes sense. we'll cover high-level architecture and then follow up with security packet.
[00:45] Tom Reyes: Quick context — we're a regional bank across EU and US, have EU customers that must stay in-EU for GDPR. also some lines of business have stricter retention/scrubbing requirements. so want to assess options.
[01:05] Priya Kapoor: Understood. do you currently have any deployed LLM infra or are you leaning to API consumption?
[01:20] Rhea Patel: We're currently experimenting with a couple of hosted providers for non-critical chat assistance, but for any PII or customer-sensitive flows we can't send data outside declared regions. procurement will push for dedicated or private if needed.
[01:38] Alex Chen: Makes sense. are there any legal/regulatory mandates explicitly forbidding us from storing logs outside region? or is it covered by contractual terms with customers?
[01:52] Liam O'Neil: It's a mix — GDPR data residency plus a handful of enterprise customers require per-contract residency and audit trail retention of six years for some records. we need confirmation on log granularities and retention tiers.
[02:10] Jordan Li: Quick clarification: when you say logs, do you mean request/response transcripts, token-level logs, or system-level audit logs?
[02:25] Karen Miles: All of the above. request-level telemetry for debugging, plus system audit logs for access. but request/response content must be treated carefully; we need ability to limit storage, redact PII, and optionally keep only structured metadata.
[02:43] Priya Kapoor: Redwood supports different persistence models — Hosted by default keeps logs for debugging but you can set redaction and retention policies; Dedicated gives you dedicated GPU pools and isolation, with stronger guarantees on data handling; Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you full control and we can disable our centralized logging if necessary.
[03:05] Tom Reyes: What about EU-only hosting for certain models? For example if we want EU residency for customer A but US for customer B. can we partition?
[03:22] Alex Chen: Yes — with routing policies you can pin requests by tenant/route to region-specific endpoints. for Hosted customers we have EU regions, for Dedicated we can provision capacity in EU zones; Private you run in your VPC.
[03:40] Rhea Patel: That routing — is it at the model level or per-request? latency-wise we can't add too much.
[03:52] Priya Kapoor: It's per-route. We use smart routing that can be tag/policy based so it happens in the control plane, minimal overhead. latency impact is typically small if endpoints are region-local. we'll share P50/P95 numbers in the follow-up.
[04:10] Karen Miles: Encryption — we need to use our own KMS/HSM for key control. does Redwood integrate with customer-managed keys?
[04:23] Jordan Li: Yes — Dedicated and Private support customer-managed KMS; Hosted can integrate with managed CMKs in some cases (cloud KMS integration), but for strict HSM requirements Private deployment is recommended.
[04:40] Liam O'Neil: Can you be explicit on what side channel / inference data is retained? e.g., KV cache, prefix caching, embeddings.
[04:50] Priya Kapoor: Good question. We don't persist KV cache across customers; caching is ephemeral in the runtime unless you opt into longer-lived caching. embeddings and long-term storage are opt-in features — they won't be stored unless you enable embedding storage. for Hosted, transcription/requests can be logged for debugging; we have redaction and opt-out controls.
[05:15] Tom Reyes: We heard some vendors keep token-level logs for telemetry even if you ask not to — is Redwood able to run with minimal logs for us?
[05:26] Alex Chen: We can run with very limited telemetry. Dedicated and Private give you the tightest control. Hosted can be configured with stricter retention and redaction, but Dedicated is usually the middle ground for customers who need both performance and stronger controls.
[05:42] Karen Miles: Audits — do you provide SOC2 Type II reports, ISO27001, penetration test summaries? we need to attach to our security vetting.
[05:52] Alex Chen: Yes, we publish SOC 2 and ISO documents; we'll send the redacted reports and a security packet. also can arrange an NDA/SAQ or in some cases a security workshop. link: https://redwood.ai/security (we'll send direct docs).
[06:10] Rhea Patel: For EU residency can Redwood guarantee that logs never leave EU for a given route?
[06:22] Priya Kapoor: For Dedicated and Private yes — you can pin compute and storage to specific regions. For Hosted we operate regionally and have EU regions that keep data in-EU, but we need to confirm any cross-region failover policies. we'll call that out in the follow-up notes.
[06:42] Liam O'Neil: Contractually we need an SLA clause about data location and an audit clause with 30-day access to logs for legal review. That may push us towards Dedicated/Private.
[06:55] Alex Chen: Understood. many customers in financial services choose Dedicated for contractual auditability and guaranteed isolation. Private is for cases where the regulator requires the infrastructure to be within customer control.
[07:10] Tom Reyes: How does Redwood handle redaction? automatic PII detection, or we need to pre-process?
[07:21] Priya Kapoor: We have built-in PII scrubbers for common patterns and you can add deterministic redaction rules. For high-assurance flows some customers pre-process or perform client-side tokenization before sending. we also support a policy to only send structured metadata back to Redwood and keep raw content on-prem.
[07:45] Karen Miles: What about logs required for fraud detection — those need to be available for 6 years sometimes. do you support tiered retention?
[07:57] Jordan Li: Yes, tiered retention is supported in Dedicated/Private with retention policies; Hosted has retention windows but longer-term archival typically comes with add-ons or requires Dedicated.
[08:12] Tom Reyes: Are there any restrictions on export of logs for investigations? we need exportable forensic bundles.
[08:21] Priya Kapoor: You can export audit bundles; for Dedicated/Private you control retention and export. Hosted supports exports under contractual terms. We'll include details in the packet.
[08:35] Liam O'Neil: HIPAA — some of our healthcare-adjacent products handle PHI, so HIPAA BAA might be relevant. Do you sign BAAs?
[08:45] Alex Chen: Redwood can sign BAAs in Dedicated/Private scenarios; Hosted BAAs are assessed case by case. We'll escalate legal to provide BAA language as a starting point.
[08:58] Rhea Patel: From an ops standpoint, what's the networking topology for Dedicated? VPC peering or private link?
[09:07] Priya Kapoor: Dedicated typically uses VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on cloud; Private on-prem supports direct install or air-gapped options. We'll send the topology diagrams.
[09:20] Tom Reyes: Any known performance differences between Hosted EU region and Dedicated EU capacity? we care about p99 for chat latency.
[09:29] Jordan Li: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and you can reserve capacity to hit lower p99s. We'll share benchmark numbers — typical Hosted P95 is X ms for our smaller seqs but Dedicated can be tuned. (Note: numbers to be provided in follow-up).
[09:47] Karen Miles: On logging granularity — if we request that request/response bodies be never stored, will you still retain hashed message digests for de-dup and telemetry?
[09:59] Priya Kapoor: You can choose to retain only hashed digests and structured metadata; raw bodies can be redacted or never persisted depending on deployment mode. we'll document options and default behaviors in the packet.
[10:18] Alex Chen: Quick pause — any blockers for procurement if we propose Dedicated as the initial pilot?
[10:25] Liam O'Neil: Procurement will want pricing and some contract language; security will need SOC2 + network topology + BAAs if applicable. timeline wise we have an RFP window in late Nov, decisions by mid-Dec.
[10:40] Alex Chen: Great — we'll aim to have the security packet and Dedicated pricing into you by Nov 11-13 to match your cadence.
[10:48] Tom Reyes: One more thing: embeddings and vector DBs — if those contain customer PII, we need to ensure embedding storage is in-region and encrypted with our keys.
[10:59] Jordan Li: Absolutely. embeddings are opt-in and we can store them in customer-controlled storage and encrypt with your KMS in Dedicated/Private. For Hosted we can offer regionally isolated embedding stores with customer-managed keys in some setups.
[11:18] Rhea Patel: Are there documented controls for who inside Redwood can access logs? we need role-based access control and audit logs for any human access.
[11:29] Priya Kapoor: We enforce RBAC, ephemeral privileged access, and all accesses are logged. in Dedicated/Private, access can be limited or run through the customer's identity provider.
[11:45] Karen Miles: If we go Dedicated, do you provide an option for customer-managed logging (push logs to our S3/GCS) so we don't have copies in Redwood?
[11:58] Alex Chen: Yes — log forwarding to customer-managed buckets is supported; you can also disable centralized logging entirely for Private deployments.
[12:10] Tom Reyes: Any difference in how function/tool-calling or chain-of-thought outputs are handled from a compliance perspective?
[12:21] Jordan Li: Those are handled similarly to response payloads — if you need to suppress certain outputs from logs we can set redaction rules or strip certain fields.
[12:35] Liam O'Neil: Ok, procurement note: we'll need an estimated cost delta between Hosted vs Dedicated for pilot usage — even a rough monthly number to present to finance.
[12:45] Alex Chen: We'll include a dedicated vs hosted cost estimate in the pricing deck.
[12:52] Karen Miles: Anything about backups and disaster recovery? we need RTO/RPO guarantees and cross-region replication policies.
[13:03] Priya Kapoor: DR is configurable; Dedicated replication can be within-region isolated or cross-region with explicit policy; for strict residency you can enable within-region failover only. We'll include RTO/RPO numbers.
[13:20] Tom Reyes: Are audit logs tamper-evident? we prefer WORM or append-only mechanisms.
[13:28] Jordan Li: We support append-only audit logs and can integrate with object lock / WORM features on major clouds for Dedicated setups.
[13:38] Rhea Patel: Performance benchmarking — can you run a small benchmark using our representative prompt set? we'd like to see latency and token-cost tradeoffs.
[13:49] Priya Kapoor: Yes, we can run a benchmark on Dedicated EU capacity or Hosted EU region. we'll need your prompt set and a small test dataset, and we'll coordinate a window for the benchmark to run.
[14:05] Alex Chen: I'll follow up to schedule and we can sign an NDA if necessary for sensitive test data.
[14:12] Liam O'Neil: Legal also wants to know about incident response — notification windows and forensics support.
[14:20] Priya Kapoor: Our incident response includes a playbook, predefined notification windows (we'll include in packet), and we can support forensics exports when on Dedicated/Private.
[14:35] Karen Miles: Are there any known limitations around GPU/quantization profiles that would affect model parity between Hosted and Dedicated?
[14:45] Jordan Li: Some lower-precision quantization kernels differ slightly between hardware types; we have verified performance profiles for common open models and can provide model parity notes. for strict parity, Private is the cleanest.
[14:58] Tom Reyes: Ok this is helpful. next steps recap?
[15:05] Alex Chen: Recap: 1) we'll send SOC2/ISO/security packet + BAA draft 2) Priya will share latency/cost matrix and deployment diagrams 3) schedule technical benchmark once Summit shares prompt set 4) provide Dedicated pricing for pilot.
[15:23] Karen Miles: Perfect. we'll get our prompt set and residency rules over by Thursday.
[15:30] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone. we'll follow up via email and drop the security packet.
[15:36] Meeting end.
